subject: Computer Networking
title: DHCP: Automatic Network Setup
description: A 60-second lesson on DHCP: Automatic Network Setup.

hook.text: You plug in a cable or join Wi-Fi. Instantly your device gets an IP address. You didn't configure anything.

buildup.text: DHCP — Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol — assigns IP addresses, gateways, and DNS servers automatically.

discovery.text: Your device broadcasts 'I need an address.' The DHCP server replies with a lease: an IP for a set time.

twist.text: Leases expire. If your device disappears, the address returns to the pool. No manual cleanup needed.

climax.text: Without DHCP, every device would need manual configuration. Large networks would be unmanageable.

punchline.text: DHCP makes joining a network effortless. It just works.

quiz.question: What does DHCP provide to a device joining a network?
options: An IP address, gateway, and DNS configuration automatically
A website's content from a CDN
An encrypted tunnel to a remote server

details.summary: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, gateways, and DNS server addresses to devices when they join a network. This eliminates manual configuration and prevents address conflicts. DHCP leases addresses temporarily, reclaiming them when devices leave the network.
details.whyItMatters: DHCP makes networks work automatically for end users. Without it, every device would need manual IP configuration, making networks impractical for anything beyond a handful of devices.
takeaways: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically when devices connect
Leases are temporary and reclaimed when devices disconnect
The four-step DORA process handles address assignment

faq.question: What is the DHCP DORA process?
faq.answer: Discover: the client broadcasts a request for an address. Offer: the DHCP server offers an available address. Request: the client accepts the offer. Acknowledge: the server confirms the lease. This four-step exchange typically completes in milliseconds when a device connects to the network.

faq.question: What happens when a DHCP lease expires?
faq.answer: Devices attempt to renew their lease at 50 percent of the lease time. If renewal fails, they try again at 87.5 percent. If the lease expires completely, the device must restart the DORA process. Short leases reclaim addresses faster but generate more DHCP traffic.
